anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: No threshold exists outside the spec, and no code path sweeps one — 'Every detector rule ... exists in docs/playbook-detector-spec.md BEFORE the code that uses it'
anti_goal_violations.evidence: OPEN — a detector RULE (not a threshold, and not a value) is settled in code rather than in the spec. docs/playbook-detector-spec.md section 3.5 names the disclosures 'decline_mbr' and 'decline_bars' without defining them, and states re-anchoring only as 'a new low after v re-anchors v'. apps/backend/app/research/desk_playbook_detect.py:_find_climax_formation and :detect_capitulation settle both: decline_bars = climax_idx - window_start + 1 (the WHOLE decline leg) and decline_mbr = (close before the vertical-move window - leg_low)/mbr, plus a concrete running-extreme re-anchoring rule that also resets the bounce-window clock. The developer disclosed this in docs/handoffs/goal-playbook-iter-5-dev.md 'Known Issues' and deliberately did NOT follow the iteration spec's own data-contract phrasing ('bars from the possibly re-anchored climax bar to leg_low's formation'), which would be degenerately zero. No threshold was invented, tuned, or swept: all five capitulation/euphoria constants and PLAYBOOK_STOP_PAD_FRAC = 0.30 were already in spec section 1 and section 3.5 (spec has a zero diff this iteration, verified by the evaluator). FIX (the iter-2 B3/B4 precedent): a documentation-only spec edit defining both disclosures and the re-anchoring rule, before J-06 adds three more detectors and J-07 back-scans real sessions.
